answer: Trust in a shared ledger does not come from the ledger itself but from the checks that let strangers confirm the same facts. The word saffron captures the first of those checks: a claim that can be tested instead of merely believed. The word umber captures the second: work that is visible to others, so participation cannot hide behind a private assertion. The word meadow captures the third: a record that remains open to review over time, letting a community keep verified entries and discard the rest.
